- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment > 1.0) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.5) — model shows lagged mean reversion, missing downward momentum.
- When sentiment swings sharply from negative to positive, model delays upward correction — forecast lags by 2–3 days.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term sentiment volatility — smooth out sharp sentiment-driven spikes in forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates late-period price increases (last 5–7 days of forecast) — especially when sentiment turns positive mid-horizon.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overforecast — apply downward bias correction by 0.5–1.5% for such cases.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model overestimates by 2–4% — apply mean reversion adjustment to bring forecast closer to recent 10-day average.
